# 1 Enoch Chapter 72 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 72 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 72:1 — 'portals' / 'gates' / 'doors' for Ge'ez mashber/mawase't

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "portals" | Traditional scholarly rendering; conveys architectural grandeur |
| LOGOS | "portals" | Retains the technical astronomical-architectural terminology |
| PNEUMA | "gates" | More accessible English; same semantic range |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'portals' (EMET/LOGOS). This is the standard scholarly term for the six horizon positions of sunrise/sunset in 1 Enoch's astronomical model. 'Gates' (PNEUMA) is acceptable but less precise in the context of this technical literature.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS. Technical terminology preserved.

---

## 72:1 — 'courses' vs. 'movements' vs. 'paths' for Ge'ez term

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "courses" | Traditional: the ordered, repetitive movements of celestial bodies |
| LOGOS | "courses" | Matches established academic translations (Charles, Nickelsburg) |
| PNEUMA | "movements" | More transparent for modern readers |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'courses' (EMET/LOGOS). The term refers to the fixed, predictable paths of the luminaries — 'courses' preserves both the regularity and the astronomical connotation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS. Both aligned.

---

## 72:4 — Structure of the solar description

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | Full Ge'ez construct-chain with hyphens | Maximum transparency to source structure |
| LOGOS | Clean prose sentences | Prioritizes English readability |
| PNEUMA | Narrative expansion | Explicates the astronomical meaning for modern readers |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS formal prose. The Astronomical Book's descriptions are already highly repetitive and technical; clean prose serves the reader without distorting the content.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Structural clarity preferred.

---

## 72:35 — The 364-day year

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the year is exactly as-to-its-days three-hundred and-sixty-four days" | Preserves Ge'ez emphasis on exactness |
| LOGOS | "the year is exactly three hundred and sixty-four days" | Same content, clean prose |
| PNEUMA | "The complete year runs exactly three hundred and sixty-four days" | 'Complete' adds English idiom to stress finality |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering. The 364-day year is the key theological claim of the Astronomical Book — it is presented as divinely ordained and exact. The number is theologically loaded: 364 = 52 weeks exactly, allowing all festivals to fall on the same day each year. This stands in polemical contrast to the 354-day lunar calendar of mainstream Judaism.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. The number's significance needs no amplification.

---
